claim_tested: AHSP accumulates in the nucleus of late erythroblasts
key_finding: AHSP cytoplasmic+nuclear in early erythroblasts, 'predominantly in the nucleus' late, expelled with the nucleus at enucleation
context: human blood and bone-marrow biphasic erythroid cultures; murine bone marrow validation; Amnis IFC + flow + RT-qPCR
confidence_limitations: Single laboratory, single modality. IFC is a widefield projection; mask-overlap scoring in a cell whose nucleus fills half the volume cannot separate nuclear from overlying cytoplasmic signal. No fractionation or confocal confirmation found.

citation: This work (computational; UniProt Q9NZD4 + 89 mammalian orthologs)
key_finding: 0 matches for Chelsky monopartite, PSORT pat4, PSORT pat7 and Robbins bipartite NLS in human AHSP and in 0 of 89 mammalian orthologs; pI 4.61, net charge -5.05, longest K/R run 1 residue (max 3 across orthologs); 89/89 orthologs net negative
confidence_limitations: Pattern scan calibrated in this work: sensitivity 63.6% on 2,151 nucleus-annotated human proteins, false-positive rate 35.9% on 676 cytosol-annotated proteins (Fisher OR 3.11, p=1.8e-36). A zero score therefore shifts the odds but does not exclude nuclear localization on its own.

claim_tested: AHSP carries a CRM1-type nuclear export signal
key_finding: 3 loose Rev/PKI regex matches, indistinguishable from a 10,000-shuffle null (mean 2.45, P(shuffled>=3)=0.44); spacing-critical hydrophobics buried (F18 RSA 0.3%, M37 3.3%, V41 3.9% vs 37.0% protein mean) inside helices H1 (4-24) and H2 (33-56)
context: free AHSP NMR structure 1W09 model 1; Shrake-Rupley SASA, 1.4 A probe, 960-point sphere
confidence_limitations: Regex-plus-accessibility argument, not a CRM1 binding assay. Applies to the folded state; a transiently unfolded AHSP was not modelled.

claim_tested: AHSP is small enough to cross the nuclear pore passively
key_finding: AHSP is 12 kDa and monomeric; forms a 1:1 complex with alpha-globin (Ka = 1e7 M-1). Computed here: 11.84 kDa monomer, 26.97 kDa complex, both far below the 40-60 kDa passive limit and the same size as GFP
context: recombinant human AHSP and alpha-globin; AUC, gel filtration, ITC
confidence_limitations: Size argument removes the need for an importin but does not explain enrichment; passive diffusion predicts equal nucleoplasmic and cytoplasmic concentration.

citation: This work (computational; closed form + Monte Carlo)
claim_tested: Nuclear condensation alone can produce the reported pattern
key_finding: At the orthochromatic stage a strictly cytoplasmic protein projects 53.1% of its signal into the nuclear mask and a passively equilibrated one 60.5%, with 47.1% of molecules genuinely inside the nucleus; both rise monotonically with maturation (41%->59% and 44%->68%)
context: concentric-sphere projection model, standard erythroblast cell/nuclear diameters; closed form validated against 2e6-point Monte Carlo
confidence_limitations: Idealised concentric geometry; real late erythroblast nuclei are eccentric. Shows the reported trend needs no import; does not prove the original observation was an artifact.

claim_tested: AHSP departs with the nucleus at enucleation
key_finding: Hemoglobin chains plus AHSP are 50% of total cellular protein at the orthochromatic stage; about 82% of cytoplasm and 61% of plasma membrane segregate with the reticulocyte at enucleation
context: human erythroid differentiation, BFU-E to orthochromatic, 6,130 proteins absolutely quantified; reticulocyte vs pyrenocyte partitioning measured
confidence_limitations: The per-protein AHSP reticulocyte/pyrenocyte ratio was not retrievable programmatically (EuropePMC supplementary endpoint returned 168 bytes; fullTextXML timed out). Quoted statements verified from PMC5274717 text.

claim_tested: AHSP is largely lost with the expelled nucleus
key_finding: AHSP is quantifiable in mature red cell lysates (0.82 ug/ml control, 2.23 ug/ml untreated sickle cell anaemia) and correlates strongly with the alpha-hemoglobin pool
context: human red blood cell lysates, n=10 control, 10 HC-treated SCA, 12 untreated SCA
confidence_limitations: Measures the post-enucleation endpoint, not the erythroblast distribution; does not quantify how much AHSP left with pyrenocytes.

claim_tested: Material leaving with the nucleus is necessarily nuclear
key_finding: Pyrenocytes are defined as nuclei with a thin rim of cytoplasm, so cytoplasmic protein inevitably co-departs with the extruded nucleus
context: mouse primitive and definitive erythroblasts; immunohistochemistry and multispectral imaging flow cytometry
confidence_limitations: Mouse primitive erythropoiesis; the principle is general but the cytoplasmic rim volume is not quantified for human definitive orthochromatic cells.

claim_tested: AHSP has a domain that would retain it in the nucleus
key_finding: Only AHSP-family entries returned (IPR015317, IPR036468, PF09236, PTHR15914, SSF109751, G3DSA:1.20.58.420); no DNA-binding, RNA-binding, chromatin or nuclear-transport domain. Zero PY dipeptides (no PY-NLS); max 4 K/R per 20-aa window (no NoLS); 3 K/R in N-terminal 45 aa (no IBB)
context: InterPro release accessed via EBI API
confidence_limitations: Absence of annotation is not proof of absence of function; AHSP is a small single-domain protein with little annotation depth.

claim_tested: Databases and the founding literature place AHSP in the nucleus
key_finding: UniProt subcellular location is Cytoplasm only (GO:0005737, IBA); no nucleus term. Discovery paper describes a soluble alpha-globin chaperone. IHC across 100 bone marrow and splenic specimens used AHSP as an erythroid-precursor marker with no nuclear pattern reported
context: database record; human/mouse erythroid cells; human bone marrow and spleen
confidence_limitations: IHC studies were not designed to score subcellular compartment; absence of a reported nuclear pattern is weak negative evidence.

claim_tested: A nuclear carrier imports AHSP by piggy-backing
key_finding: Only HBA (P69905) is well supported; CLVS1, FKBP1A, PSMB1, UBE3A-2, VPS9D1, ZC3H12A and ZNF20 each rest on ~3 experiments typical of one high-throughput two-hybrid screen, and none is an erythroid nuclear protein with in vivo support
context: curated interaction records, mostly non-erythroid high-throughput screens
confidence_limitations: The erythroid AHSP interactome has not been determined by AP-MS in erythroblasts, so a carrier cannot be excluded.

key_finding: Subcellular main location 'Not available'; cell analysis 'Pending'. No immunofluorescence localization available
confidence_limitations: Genuine absence of data, retrieved 2026-11; not evidence either way.
